title: Heavy Rain Lashes Delhi-NCR as IMD Issues Red Alert for Several Districts
excerpt: Intense monsoon downpours bring waterlogging, traffic snarls, and thunderstorm warnings across the national capital region, with more rain expected through August 27.
body:
• The India Meteorological Department has issued red and orange alerts for multiple Delhi districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and lightning.
  • Widespread waterlogging and traffic congestion have been reported across Delhi-NCR, with key routes including Ring Road, Outer Ring Road, and NH-48 severely affected.
  • The monsoon spell is driven by multiple active weather systems over northern India, with IMD forecasting continued rainfall through August 27.
  • Heavy rain alerts extend across multiple states including Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, and parts of southern India.

Monsoon Intensifies Over National Capital

Delhi and the National Capital Region were battered by heavy monsoon rain over the weekend, prompting the India Meteorological Department to issue red alerts for several districts as thunderstorms and intense downpours disrupted daily life across the city.

The IMD upgraded its warnings from yellow to orange and then to red alert, signaling "extremely heavy rainfall" and advising residents to avoid unnecessary travel. Red alerts were issued for New Delhi, Southwest Delhi, Southeast Delhi, and South Delhi, while orange alerts covered North Delhi, Northwest Delhi, West Delhi, Central Delhi, East Delhi, Northeast Delhi, and the Shahdara region.

Delhi, Noida, Gurugram, and Ghaziabad experienced intense spells of rain accompanied by lightning and gusty winds. Residents have been advised to remain prepared for sudden changes in weather conditions as the active monsoon phase continues.

Waterlogging Cripples Roads and Transit

Severe waterlogging was reported from multiple areas across the capital, including Sadar Bazar, Nasirpur, Greater Kailash, Badarpur, Teliwara, Mahavir Bazar, Swarup Nagar, and Kushak Road. Traffic slowed to a crawl on Ring Road, Outer Ring Road, and NH-48, particularly near Dhaula Kuan, Mahipalpur, and Rajokri.

Traffic snarls were also reported on Mehrauli-Badarpur Road, ITO, Wazirabad Road, Patel Road, Rohtak Road, Shankar Road, the Kirti Nagar stretch, the Delhi-Jaipur Highway, and Peeragarhi. In east Delhi, congestion built up on GT Road, GTB Enclave, and Dilshad Garden.

Neighboring Gurugram saw vehicles stranded on waterlogged roads, with severe congestion reported on the Delhi-Jaipur Highway service lane near Narsinghpur, Basai, Umang Bhardwaj Chowk, Kadipur, Sector 10A, and Sohna Road. The Delhi Fire Service responded to multiple calls about uprooted trees in East of Kailash and other areas.

More Rain Forecast Through the Week

The IMD attributed the ongoing spell to a rare combination of multiple weather systems active over northern India. Forecasts indicate generally cloudy skies for Delhi with continued spells of light to moderate rain, along with isolated heavy rainfall and thunderstorms through August 27.

Maximum temperatures in Delhi are expected to remain between 31 and 33 degrees Celsius, with minimum temperatures between 22 and 24 degrees Celsius. Surface winds are expected at 10-15 kmph.

Both the IMD and private forecaster Skymet have predicted that the heaviest and most widespread rain will fall between August 23 and 25, with active monsoon conditions expected to persist across the country until at least August 27.

Nationwide Monsoon Impact

The Delhi rainfall is part of a broader monsoon pattern affecting much of India. Heavy to very heavy rainfall has been forecast for Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha. Several northeastern states are also experiencing significant rainfall.

In southern India, the IMD has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka, with very heavy rainfall possible in isolated pockets. Thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds are expected across parts of Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh.

The IMD has urged residents across affected regions to remain cautious, avoid waterlogged areas, and monitor weather updates regularly as the monsoon maintains its intensity across the subcontinent.
